prompt: Which oxidation of a 2° alcohol gives a KETONE (not over-oxidation)?

options.label: Na₂Cr₂O₇ / H₂SO₄ / H₂O — 2° alcohols stop at ketone (no α-H on the C=O to re-oxidize)
All oxidations go all the way to COOH
The ketone is not stable; it hydrates

explanation: Oxidation of a 2° alcohol gives a ketone, and the ketone has no C–H bond on the carbonyl C to further oxidize. Chromium, Jones, and PCC all work. 1° alcohols with aqueous Cr(VI) over-oxidize (through aldehyde hydrate) to COOH.
